angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,057,464 km at 136.29 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.3373 +/- 0.0181 mas (same row, RUWE 1.12): 136.29 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.52 +/- 0.07 solar radii from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-38 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract): 1,057,464 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.76 +/- 0.28 solar masses from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-38 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6180 +/- 50 K from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-38 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-38 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-38.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.320, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
